status: COMPLETE — all of §0–§15 + Defaults table + Source ledger captured in mm-1..mm-63 (research read in full; no context dropped). sections_accounted maps every section to its rules.
note: Faithful rule manifest for LLM memory management, distilled from MNEME_MEMORY_RESEARCH.md (Parts A/B/C) and bound to MNEME_MEMORY_SPEC.md (design of record). The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with predicate/reviewer_criterion. Mneme applies this when storing/recalling/consolidating/superseding/merging/validating memory. Rules tagged [DESIGN] encode the binding spec; the .db-vs-.jsonl source-of-truth tension (mm-52) is surfaced, not silently resolved.

rules.text: Model memory as a six-phase lifecycle — Write→Store→Retrieve→Execute→Share→Forget — crossed with four objectives (Integrity, Confidentiality, Availability, Governance). The strongest correctness/safety mitigations act at WRITE time: content never written can't be extracted; content retained indefinitely almost certainly will be. (Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty, arXiv 2604.16548.)

The single most important correctness feature for a long-lived agent: UPDATE = supersede, don't blind-append; invalidate, don't delete — new knowledge retires old while history survives. (Mem0 UPDATE/DELETE 2504.19413; Zep edge invalidation 2501.13956.)

The vector DB stays the recall engine; structure ((subject,relation,object), bi-temporal validity, provenance) is ADDED METADATA layered on top of semantic search, NOT a replacement for it. Recall must still work via vector even for unstructured rows. [DESIGN, spec §1]

predicate.spec: the design retains vector similarity as the recall engine; structured fields are additive metadata; unstructured rows are still recallable via embeddings — no swap to a pure graph/relational store.

rules.text: Use the CoALA four-type taxonomy (arXiv 2309.02427): working (context/scratchpad, one session), episodic (time-stamped events, cross-session), semantic (decontextualized facts, cross-session, updated), procedural (how-to/rules/skills, slowly changing).

predicate.spec: every memory is assigned one of {working, episodic, semantic, procedural} per the CoALA definitions.

rules.text: Know the orthogonal axis (survey 2505.00675): parametric (in weights) vs contextual (external text/KG/tables); agent memory here is CONTEXTUAL. Know the human-memory roots: Atkinson–Shiffrin (context=STM/DB=LTM), Baddeley working memory, Tulving episodic/semantic/procedural, Complementary Learning Systems (episodic→semantic consolidation).

Apply the taxonomy per-type: SEMANTIC gets full (subject,relation,object) + bi-temporal + supersession (conflicts live here); EPISODIC is immutable, decay-eligible, NO supersession (events accumulate, don't contradict); PROCEDURAL is superseded by a newer rule for the same subject, key = (subject, relation='rule', object). [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: semantic rows carry S/R/O+bitemporal+supersession; episodic rows are immutable & never superseded; procedural rows supersede by (subject, relation='rule').

rules.text: Express all memory behavior as six atomic operations: store, recall, consolidate, merge, validate, serialize/deserialize (underlying primitives: consolidate/update/index/forget/retrieve/compress).

predicate.spec: the memory surface is decomposed into exactly store/recall/consolidate/merge/validate/serialize-deserialize.

rules.text: STORE generally = extract salient facts then update-against-existing (dedup/merge/supersede), NOT blind-append, then index (embeddings+BM25+graph). In THIS design the agent hot-path store is LIGHT: raw text+type+scope+provenance, content-hash id, embed, then exact-hash gate → top-k≥0.95 vector → UPDATE/NOOP else ADD; NO extraction on the hot path (that is Mneme's decoupled job). [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: hot-path store does exact-hash gate → ≥0.95 vector → UPDATE/NOOP/ADD with content-hash id + embed, and performs no LLM extraction; extraction is deferred to Mneme.

rules.text: RECALL = dense (cosine) + sparse (BM25) [+ graph] then RERANK with multi-signal ranking (recency+importance+relevance). Never pure vector.

predicate.spec: recall combines dense+sparse retrieval and a rerank/multi-signal step; it is not vector-only.

rules.text: CONSOLIDATE = summarize + reflect (insights from episode clusters) + fact-extraction + conflict resolution (episodic→semantic, invalidate superseded) + forget/decay + tier promotion; run as light hot-path writes + heavy background ('subconscious') consolidation — never block responding on heavy consolidation.

predicate.spec: consolidation covers summarize/reflect/extract/resolve-conflicts/forget/promote and runs in the background, not on the response path.

rules.text: Foundational blueprints: Generative Agents (2304.03442) — memory stream + reflection tree; retrieval score = α_recency·recency + α_importance·importance + α_relevance·relevance (min-max normalized; recency=exp decay ~0.99–0.995 on last-access; importance=LLM 1–10 poignancy; relevance=cosine); reflection triggers at Σ recent importance ~150. CoALA (2309.02427) — reference taxonomy + decision loop; learning = writing to episodic/semantic/procedural memory.

Framework landscape: MemGPT/Letta 2310.08560 (virtual context paging, inspectable memory blocks); Mem0 2504.19413 (extract→update, ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP; Mem0^g invalidate-not-delete); Zep+Graphiti 2501.13956 (bi-temporal KG, 4 timestamps, LLM edge-invalidation, non-lossy); A-MEM 2502.12110 (Zettelkasten, link-generation+memory-evolution, multi-hop); LangMem/LangGraph (BaseStore, namespaced by user_id, hot-path vs background, prompt-optimizer procedural); Cognee (ECL→graph+vector, GraphRAG); MemoryOS 2506.06326 (STM/MTM/LPM heat-scored); Titans 2501.00663 (parametric test-time weight writes + surprise + adaptive forgetting); MemoryBank 2305.10250 (Ebbinghaus forgetting curve); HippoRAG (NeurIPS 2024, OpenIE KG + Personalized PageRank multi-hop).

Match the pattern to the problem: inspectable self-managed context→Letta/MemGPT; cheap fast fact-memory→Mem0; evolving/contradictory/time-sensitive+audit→Zep/Graphiti; emergent multi-hop w/o schema→A-MEM; three types+hot/background→LangMem; ontology-KG from docs→Cognee; parametric/test-time→Titans. This system is a deliberate hybrid: Mem0-style fact ops + Zep-style bi-temporal supersession over a sqlite-vec recall engine.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is the chosen memory pattern justified against the problem's needs (fact-memory vs evolving/temporal+audit vs multi-hop vs ontology), rather than picked by default — and is this system framed as Mem0-fact-ops + Zep-bitemporal over sqlite-vec?

rules.text: Representation is the biggest lever: raw text (lossless, fuzzy retrieval, tokens grow) vs extracted facts (compact, weakens multi-hop/temporal) vs KG (multi-hop/temporal/relational, costly+drift). Counter-current: verbatim chunks can BEAT lossy extraction — never assume graph/extraction is strictly better; always keep the raw text so re-embedding/re-extraction stay possible.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is the representation choice reasoned per workload (not assumed 'graph/extraction is better'), and is the raw text retained so re-embedding/re-extraction remain possible?

rules.text: Temporal modeling is first-class — model bi-temporal validity (world-valid time separate from system-transaction time), not a single timestamp, whenever facts can change.

predicate.spec: changeable facts carry two time axes (world valid_from/valid_to and system ingested_at/expired_at), not a single timestamp.

rules.text: Consolidation timing — combine light hot-path writes (immediate, minimal latency/budget) with heavy background consolidation (fast responses, eventual consistency). Do not run heavy consolidation on the response path.

predicate.spec: heavy consolidation runs asynchronously/in-background; the response path only does light writes.

rules.text: Namespacing/isolation is non-negotiable in multi-user/multi-agent — scope every read and write (here scope = agent_id). Cross-scope bleed is a privacy failure.

predicate.spec: every read and write is filtered by scope (agent_id); no query can return another scope's rows.

rules.text: Provenance/auditability — every derived fact keeps a link back to its source ('why do you believe this?'): derived_from / source / evidence.

predicate.spec: derived facts populate derived_from/source/evidence linking to their origin; orphaned-provenance is flagged by validate.

rules.text: Forgetting is a feature — unbounded memory hurts BOTH cost and retrieval precision (distractors). Design decay/heat-eviction/importance-pruning/TTL deliberately; a store with no forgetting mechanism is a defect.

predicate.spec: the store implements at least one deliberate forgetting mechanism (decay, heat-eviction, importance-pruning, or TTL).

rules.text: Benchmark integrity — LOCOMO / LongMemEval (2410.10813) / DMR are the benchmarks; NEVER repeat an 'X% better' number without naming who measured it and the config (vendor benchmarks are marketing until independently reproduced; Mem0-vs-Zep numbers were disputed and corrected; LOCOMO has annotation-noise criticism).

predicate.spec: any cited benchmark delta is accompanied by an attribution (who measured) and config; vendor numbers are labelled vendor-measured; reject bare 'X% better' claims.

rules.text: The id is content-addressed = sha256(normalized_text + type + scope), NOT a random UUID → idempotent, order-independent dedup + cross-machine sync. Here content_id = sha256(normalized_text + type + agent_id). [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: the record id/content_id equals sha256(normalized_text + type + scope/agent_id); it is not a random UUID.

rules.text: The embedding contract is ONE atomic unit stored per record: embedding + embedding_model + embedding_version + dim + metric + normalized.

predicate.spec: each record stores embedding + embedding_model + embedding_version + dim + metric + normalized together.

rules.text: Store bi-temporal fields: valid_from/valid_to (world-truth window) SEPARATE from ingested_at/expired_at (system learned/retracted). Active ⇔ valid_to IS NULL AND expired_at IS NULL — this is what lets you supersede without deleting.

predicate.spec: records carry valid_from/valid_to and ingested_at/expired_at as distinct fields; active-set = valid_to IS NULL AND expired_at IS NULL.

rules.text: Round out the row: subject/relation/object (nullable for episodic and until structured); lifecycle (created_at, last_used_at, use_count, importance 1–10); provenance/trust (source, principal, asserted_by∈{user,agent-inferred}, confidence, evidence); links (supersedes/superseded_by/derived_from, content_hash); FTS5 shadow table over text(+subject/object) for BM25. [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: the record has subject/relation/object, created_at/last_used_at/use_count/importance, source/principal/asserted_by/confidence/evidence, supersedes/superseded_by/derived_from/content_hash, and an FTS5 shadow table exists for BM25.

rules.text: Deduplicate in three layers: exact = SHA-256 of normalized text (lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip markup); near-dup = MinHash/SimHash (LSH) for paraphrases/templates; semantic = cosine threshold/clustering. Batch semantic dedup via SemDeDup (2303.09540): k-means then keep item closest to centroid.

predicate.spec: dedup has an exact-hash layer, a near-dup LSH layer, and a semantic/cosine-clustering layer.

rules.text: Dedup thresholds (cosine, unit-norm) are defaults to sweep, never blindly hardcode: ≥0.95 = write-path 'same → UPDATE/NOOP'; 0.85–0.92 = consolidation batch dedup; 0.70 too aggressive. Apply exact-hash + conservative ≥0.95 on WRITE; reserve aggressive clustering/LLM-merge for BACKGROUND consolidation.

predicate.spec: write-path dedup uses cosine ≥0.95; batch/background dedup uses 0.85–0.92; thresholds are configurable/calibrated, not hardcoded at 0.70.

rules.text: Where an LLM is available, prefer Mem0 arbitration over a fixed threshold: retrieve top-s≈10 similar → LLM tool call returns ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP. The threshold is a cheap gate; the LLM is the precise arbiter.
rules.reviewer_criterion: For write-time dedup/merge, is the cosine threshold used only as a candidate gate with an LLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP arbiter making the final call (not a threshold deciding alone)?

rules.text: GOTCHA — high cosine can mean CONTRADICTION ('I like tea' vs 'I hate tea' embed close). Route the near-but-not-identical band (0.80 ≤ cos < 0.95) to the contradiction check (§9), NOT to the trash.

predicate.spec: the 0.80 ≤ cos < 0.95 band is routed to contradiction detection, never auto-merged/discarded as a duplicate.

rules.text: Trigger reflection by importance, not the clock: when Σ importance of recent events > ~150, take ~100 recent → LLM asks ~3 salient questions → retrieve → synthesize insights → STORE insights as new retrievable memories → hierarchical reflection tree. (Generative Agents 2304.03442.)

predicate.spec: reflection is triggered by Σ recent importance (~150), synthesizes insights, and stores them as new retrievable memories (event-driven, not clock-driven).

rules.text: Decouple consolidation from responding — run a separate consolidator in idle time ('sleep-time compute', Letta; reported ~5× less test-time compute, ~2.5× lower per-query cost). Mneme is that decoupled consolidator.

predicate.spec: consolidation runs in a separate/idle-time process (Mneme), decoupled from the responding agent.

rules.text: NEVER destroy the source when summarizing — derive semantic/summary memories carrying derived_from back to raw episodics (Zep non-lossy). Consolidate by entity/topic, not time-window alone. Make consolidation idempotent (key off content-hash + superseded_by) so re-runs don't duplicate.

predicate.spec: summaries link derived_from to retained sources (no source destroyed); consolidation groups by entity/topic and is idempotent under re-run.

rules.text: recency = decay^(hours since LAST ACCESS), decay ≈ 0.995 — decay by access, not creation; retrieval reinforces (update last_used_at/use_count on every recall). 'Use it or lose it.' (MemoryBank 2305.10250.)

predicate.spec: recency uses ~0.995^hours-since-last-access and every recall updates last_used_at/use_count.

rules.text: Score staying-power as strength = w_r·recency + w_f·log(1+access_count) + w_i·importance_norm (defaults w_r=1, w_f=0.5, w_i=1).

predicate.spec: strength = w_r·recency + w_f·log(1+access_count) + w_i·importance_norm with the stated default weights.

rules.text: Golden rule — tier + archive, NEVER hard-delete semantic facts: move low-strength to a cold tier (retrievable on deep search); supersede via valid_to/t_invalid (keep the row). Hard-delete ONLY exact duplicates, expired TTL scratch, or explicit user 'forget X'.

predicate.spec: semantic facts are tiered/archived not hard-deleted; hard-delete is restricted to exact dups, expired TTL scratch, or explicit user forget.

rules.text: KILLER FINDING — you CANNOT detect staleness/contradiction by embedding similarity: cosine AUROC for contradiction-vs-duplicate = 0.59 (≈ chance), max precision 0.67; contradictions embed MORE similar than rephrased duplicates; similarity-only RAG serves superseded values 15–40% of the time. NEVER gate supersession or the conflict decision on a similarity threshold alone. (MemStrata 2606.26511; STALE 2605.06527.) [VERIFIED]

predicate.spec: no code path decides supersession or contradiction by an embedding-similarity threshold alone; similarity is only a candidate-generation signal.

rules.text: SOTA staleness fix = DETERMINISTIC supersession keyed by (subject,relation,object): on a new value for an existing (scope,subject,relation) key, retire the prior active row in the bi-temporal ledger — NO similarity, NO LLM. Here supersede_by_key(agent_id,subject,relation,new_valid_from) sets prior active row valid_to=new_valid_from and KEEPS the row. Yields ~0.95–1.00 accuracy (vs similarity-RAG 0.20–0.47) and superseded-serve→~0%. [VERIFIED + DESIGN]

predicate.spec: supersession is a deterministic key-collision on (scope,subject,relation) that sets old.valid_to=new.valid_from and keeps the row, with no similarity threshold and no LLM call.

rules.text: Conflict = SEMANTIC CONTRADICTION only — two ACTIVE facts, SAME (agent,subject,relation), DIFFERENT object, overlapping validity ('ball is blue' vs 'ball is green'). Structure/keys/ordering/metadata are NOT conflicts. (Atiqul verbatim.) [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: a conflict is flagged only for two active facts with same (agent,subject,relation) and different object over overlapping validity; structural/key/ordering differences are never flagged as conflicts.

rules.text: Generate contradiction CANDIDATES by key-collision + vector-neighbourhood, then judge: (1) candidates = same-(subject,relation) key OR high-cosine (≳0.80) below the exact-dup cutoff; (2) an LLM/NLI judge over (new,candidate) → {entails, contradicts, neutral}. Candidate generation is key-collision + neighbourhood; the decision is never similarity-alone.

predicate.spec: contradiction candidates come from key-collision OR ≳0.80 neighbourhood, then an LLM/NLI judge classifies entails/contradicts/neutral; similarity never decides alone.

rules.text: Resolve contradictions per-case, never globally hardcoded: SUPERSEDE (new is newer state, same relation, new.valid_from>old → set old.valid_to; keep row); KEEP-BOTH (both can be true — different validity/scope or low confidence — default when unsure); ASK-HUMAN (low confidence OR high importance OR identity/safety-critical — never silently pick).
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is each contradiction resolved by a per-case choice among supersede / keep-both / ask-human (with keep-both as the unsure default and ask-human for low-confidence/high-importance/identity-safety), rather than one hardcoded global rule?

rules.text: Human-in-the-loop is the correct mitigation for the hard cases (even LLM judgment is imperfect). Mneme flags genuine contradictions in an HTML report (user given the full path), discusses until resolved, then applies the resolution (supersede one / keep-both-scoped / edit). This is the validate/merge conflict path. [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: genuine contradictions are surfaced to the user via an HTML report (full path given) and resolved by the human before Mneme applies the chosen resolution — not auto-resolved silently.

rules.text: Retrieval is HYBRID — dense (cosine) + sparse (BM25); vector alone under-recalls names, ids, and exact tokens.

predicate.spec: recall runs both a dense (cosine) and a sparse (BM25) retriever; not vector-only.

rules.text: Fuse rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion Σ 1/(k+rank), k=60 (rank-based, scale-free, industry default); use min-max score fusion (Weaviate relativeScoreFusion) only when score margins must be preserved.

predicate.spec: dense and sparse rankings are fused with RRF at k=60 (or an explicitly justified score-fusion alternative).

rules.text: Re-score with the composite prior α_rel·relevance + α_rec·recency + α_imp·importance (each min-max normalized; recency=decay^Δhours, 0.995), then apply a validity filter (active rows only, unless the query is explicitly historical). Bump last_used_at/use_count on served rows.

predicate.spec: fused results are re-scored by the composite relevance+recency+importance prior, then filtered to active rows (unless historical), and served rows get last_used_at/use_count bumped.

rules.text: Diversify with MMR: argmax[λ·rel − (1−λ)·max sim-to-already-selected], λ ≈ 0.7 — stops the top-N from becoming five paraphrases of one fact.

predicate.spec: the result set is diversified with MMR at λ≈0.7 before final selection.

rules.text: Avoid over-recall: cap injected context to a token budget, enforce an absolute similarity FLOOR (drop < ~0.2–0.3 even if top-k), and favor precision over recall for injected context. Full pipeline: BM25+cosine → RRF(60) → composite re-score → validity filter → MMR(0.7) → top-N under budget + floor → optional cross-encoder rerank.

predicate.spec: the retrieval pipeline applies a token budget cap and an absolute similarity floor (~0.2–0.3) and follows BM25+cosine→RRF(60)→composite→validity→MMR(0.7)→top-N order.

rules.text: Normalize embeddings to unit L2 at BOTH write and query — then cosine and L2 give identical rankings; sqlite-vec KNN is L2-oriented so normalizing makes L2-KNN==cosine (server already L2-normalizes). Metric must match the model's training (modern embedders → cosine/dot). sqlite-vec vec_distance_cosine is float32/int8 only and errors on mismatched type/length — store dim + element type consistently.

predicate.spec: embeddings are unit-L2-normalized at write and query, the distance metric matches the embedder's training, and dim/element-type are stored consistently.

rules.text: The embedding contract {model,version,preprocessing,normalization,metric} is ONE atomic unit — change any part → version bump → RE-EMBED THE WHOLE STORE. NEVER mix embedding generations in one index (silent recall degradation, no error); even an unchanged API model-string can hide new vectors. Version-stamp every embedding and REFUSE to serve a mixed-model index. On migration re-embed the whole corpus (blue-green) or use a learned Drift-Adapter (95–99% recall, 2509.23471); keep raw text so re-embedding stays possible.

predicate.spec: every embedding is version-stamped; the index refuses to serve mixed embedding generations; a contract change triggers a full re-embed (or Drift-Adapter) with raw text retained.

rules.text: Run a drift canary in validate: re-embed canary texts and compare to stored — <0.001 stable · 0.001–0.02 minor · 0.02–0.05 significant · >0.05 severe → re-embed all; also check nearest-neighbor stability. Monitor recall against a golden set on a schedule.

predicate.spec: validate re-embeds canary texts and applies the <0.001/0.001–0.02/0.02–0.05/>0.05 thresholds (re-embed all above 0.05), checks NN stability, and recall is monitored vs a golden set.

rules.text: Merge is UNION WITH RECONCILIATION, not concatenation — reuse ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP over content-addressed ids (same fact on two machines collides to one row; order-independent). Algorithm: exact-hash → NOOP; ≥0.95 near-dup → UPDATE (keep higher importance, union access_count); contradiction → supersede via bi-temporal (keep both histories); else ADD.

predicate.spec: merge reconciles via ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP on content ids: exact→NOOP, ≥0.95→UPDATE (max importance, union access_count), contradiction→bi-temporal supersede, else ADD — not a concat.

rules.text: Cross-machine conflict = a contradiction with a different source → resolve by bi-temporal supersession so both histories survive. Last-writer-wins is allowed ONLY for single-valued profile fields, NEVER for the append-only collection.

predicate.spec: cross-source contradictions supersede bi-temporally (both histories kept); last-writer-wins is confined to single-valued profile fields, never the collection.

rules.text: The JSONL mirror is append-only, one object per line, DETERMINISTICALLY ordered with stable key order → clean git diffs and line-level merges; carries full contract metadata (model/version per record) and re-embeds on import if the contract differs.

predicate.spec: the JSONL mirror is append-only one-object-per-line, deterministically ordered with stable key order, carries per-record model/version, and re-embeds on import when the contract differs.

rules.text: .db (sqlite-vec) is the source of truth; .jsonl is the derived mirror (Atiqul's decision). DOCUMENTED TENSION: best-practice literature (LangMem, merge/sync) treats JSONL as the sync source of truth and the vector DB as a rebuildable index — the OPPOSITE. Both coexist; 'which is authoritative on a conflicting pull' is a real open decision. Present it; do NOT flip it silently. [DESIGN]
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is .db treated as the source of truth and .jsonl as the derived mirror per the spec, AND is the opposite literature convention (JSONL-as-truth) surfaced as an open decision rather than silently applied?

rules.text: Treat EVERY write as a privileged, validated state transition — writable memory is a persistent attack surface. Poisoning is stealthy: MINJA 2503.03704 (query-only, >95% injection/>70% ASR, moderation ineffective), AgentPoison (<0.1% poison rate), MemoryGraft 2512.16962 (procedural/experience via benign README/task-log, no trigger), MemMorph 2605.26154 (85.9% ASR, 3 records). Mitigate: generate-then-freeze with human/policy verification for durable writes; provenance on every record (source, principal, version, sensitivity, time); never trust retrieved/tool/other-agent claims at user-fact level; principal-scoped access; adaptive-attacker testing.

predicate.spec: durable writes are validated (generate-then-freeze + provenance: source/principal/version/sensitivity/time), retrieved/tool/other-agent content is not trusted at user-fact level, access is principal-scoped, and adaptive-attacker tests exist.

rules.text: Do not store hallucinations as durable facts — they arise at extraction/update and propagate to QA, so gate at WRITE not answer time (HaluMem 2511.03506: fabrication, errors, conflicts, omissions). Verify before persist; record asserted_by (user vs model-inferred) + confidence + evidence in the record; never let a summarizer mint facts silently (store as type=summary, unverified, linked to source).

predicate.spec: writes are verified before persist; asserted_by/confidence/evidence are recorded; summarizer-minted facts are stored as type=summary/unverified linked to source, not as plain facts.

rules.text: NEVER store credentials/secrets/keys/PII — write-time minimization beats store-time encryption. Irreversibly mask secrets, store 'credential present at <ref>'; redact PII at write. Use retention tiers (audit-mandatory/operational/user-deletable) + TTL; lineage tracking so deletes CASCADE to summaries/derivatives; a user-visible memory inventory; monitor tool/inter-agent channels (they leak). Unlearning is imperfect — a weights backstop, not the runtime control.

predicate.spec: no credential/secret/PII value is persisted (masked to 'credential present at <ref>', PII redacted at write); retention tiers+TTL, cascading lineage deletes, and a user-visible inventory exist.

rules.text: Fight bloat/context-pollution — over-store AND over-recall both degrade reasoning before the window fills (MemGuard 2605.28009; Mem0). Precision > recall at injection: consolidate near-dups into UPDATEs; type-separate memory (facts vs episodic vs rules vs procedures) and retrieve within type; scope by user/topic/time; store salient facts not raw chunks; budget injected context.

predicate.spec: memory is type-separated with within-type retrieval, near-dups are consolidated into UPDATEs, retrieval is scoped and budgeted, and injection favors precision over recall.

rules.text: Avoid catastrophic forgetting — binary keep-all/lose-all is wrong (FadeMem 2601.18642; SSGM 2603.11768). Use differential decay by relevance+frequency+recency+importance; pin/protect critical memories (safety, identity, audit tier) from decay/consolidation; make consolidation a reversible UPDATE with content-addressable snapshots (rollback); decouple memory-evolution from execution (never let a live task rewrite durable memory).

predicate.spec: decay is differential (relevance+frequency+recency+importance), critical/safety/identity/audit memories are pinned from decay/consolidation, consolidation is reversible via content-addressable snapshots, and memory-evolution is decoupled from live execution.

rules.text: Evaluate across the WHOLE lifecycle, not just final QA. Benchmarks: LongMemEval 2410.10813 (extract/multi-session/temporal/knowledge-update/abstention), LoCoMo (multi-session QA; saturation risk), HaluMem (op-level hallucination), STALE 2605.06527 (belief revision: State Resolution/Premise Resistance/Implicit Policy Adaptation). Watch MemDelta (eval confounds — hold k/model/prompt fixed).

predicate.spec: evaluation spans extraction/multi-session/temporal/knowledge-update/abstention/belief-revision using LongMemEval/LoCoMo/HaluMem/STALE with k/model/prompt held fixed.

rules.text: Track the lifecycle metrics: recall/precision@k, MRR/nDCG, injected-context precision; op-level extraction/update accuracy; knowledge-update + temporal accuracy; superseded-serve rate (~0% TARGET); contradiction rate; abstention rate; ISR/ASR under red-team; tokens/conversation, p95 retrieval latency, storage, ingestion→retrieval delay. Validate the LLM judge against humans.

predicate.spec: the metric set includes recall/precision@k, MRR/nDCG, op-level accuracy, superseded-serve rate (~0% target), contradiction/abstention rate, red-team ISR/ASR, and latency/storage; the LLM judge is validated vs humans.

rules.text: Division of labour: the SERVER does storage + embeddings + retrieval (NO generative LLM); MNEME is the LLM-driven, DECOUPLED specialist that extracts/structures/dedupes/supersedes/consolidates and owns the conflict conversation; OTHER AGENTS store raw memories fast (light hot-path). [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: the server contains no generative LLM (storage/embeddings/retrieval only); Mneme owns extraction/structuring/dedup/supersession/consolidation/conflict; other agents only do the light hot-path store.

rules.text: Mneme STRUCTURES ON WRITE, SYNCHRONOUSLY — it structures the moment an agent writes: extracts (subject,relation,object), refines type, rates importance 1–10. Schema allows S-R-O nullable until structured so a write is never lost if structuring is momentarily pending; recall still works via vector meanwhile. Exact mechanism decided at P3. [DESIGN]

predicate.spec: structuring (S/R/O + type + importance 1–10 by Mneme) happens synchronously on write, with S-R-O nullable-until-structured so no write is lost and recall works via vector in the interim.
